description: Trigger and behaviour evals. Trigger cases assert the skill is selected; behaviour cases assert it does the right thing once selected.

should_trigger: build the mobile version of this screen
scale this mobile design up to desktop
set up a fluid type scale for this project
our text is tiny on mobile, can you fix the scale
turn this Figma desktop frame into a responsive layout
why does this table look broken at 768px
we have a 390 and a 1440 frame, wire up the tokens
check our contrast is accessible at mobile sizes
this column is supposed to be 44px but it renders wider
should_not_trigger: write a React component for a dropdown
what is the difference between rem and em
write unit tests for the cart reducer

behaviour.name: detects before asking
behaviour.given: a project that already contains a fluid-tokens.css
expect: runs scripts/detect.mjs before asking any question
reports the recovered anchors rather than asking what they are
presents remaining questions with detected defaults

behaviour.name: labels a derived anchor
behaviour.given: only a desktop Figma frame exists
expect: states explicitly that the mobile anchor is derived, not measured
presents the derived values as proposals for a designer to confirm
does not present derived numbers as though they came from a design

behaviour.name: reads both frames when both exist
behaviour.given: both a 390px and a 1440px Figma frame
expect: reads real values from both frames
does not invent or round either end
runs sweep.mjs afterwards to check for band collisions

behaviour.name: asks the nav content question
behaviour.given: a desktop design with a sidebar, deriving mobile
expect: asks whether the mobile nav is the same list as desktop
treats promotion/demotion as a product decision, not a layout one

behaviour.name: refuses to clamp a floor
behaviour.given: a request to make tap targets scale with the viewport
expect: declines to put the tap target inside a clamp()
explains that a clamped 44px target is under 44px at every width below the top anchor
offers min-height plus fluid padding instead

behaviour.name: judges contrast at the minimum anchor
behaviour.given: a token running 16px to 18px on a mid-grey
expect: requires 4.5:1, not 3:1
names it as a fluid trap
does not use the desktop size to pick the threshold

behaviour.name: requires a question per breakpoint
behaviour.given: a request to add a breakpoint at 640px
expect: asks what question the breakpoint answers
suggests a clamp() if the value is scalar
adds it to the profile registry if genuinely structural

behaviour.name: validates after generating
expect: runs sweep.mjs and contrast.mjs after generate.mjs
reports failures verbatim rather than paraphrasing
fixes the profile and regenerates rather than editing generated CSS
